children: According to Sina Finance, U.S. President Donald Trump said on Saturday that he was willing to work with Democrats in the next Congress on a one-year cap setting credit card interest rates at 10%. He said credit card companies charge excessive fees and interest, and that consumers should not have to bear those costs.

New York Fed data show U.S. credit card debt has reached a record $1.29 trillion, up 67% since early 2021. Trump first proposed a one-year 10% cap on Truth Social in January this year, saying the Biden administration had allowed rates to rise as high as 20% to 30%. Republican Senator Josh Hawley of Missouri and Democratic Senator Elizabeth Warren of Massachusetts supported the proposal. Banking associations warned that a 10% cap could restrict credit, particularly for consumers with lower credit scores, and push borrowers toward more expensive alternatives. The proposal could receive renewed attention when Democrats take control of Congress next January, and several lawmakers have voiced support for limiting credit card rates.

title: Trump Says He Is Open to Bipartisan Talks on a 10% Credit Card Rate Cap
